family: LISTING, REGISTRATION, DEREGISTRATION AND EMPLOYEE EQUITY PLANS

forms.plain_english: Short Exchange Act registration of a class of securities on a national exchange under Section 12(b). Issuers file one for each new listed class: common stock at IPO, and every series of listed notes or preferred. It incorporates the prospectus by reference, so the filing is a one-page pointer listing title, coupon, maturity and exchange.
forms.who_files_when: Issuer, on or just before the day the securities are admitted to listing (effective on exchange certification, Rule 12d1-3). Filed with the exchange's CERT same day or next day. No fixed schedule; one per listed debt offering. Observed: Amazon 2 in 2026, Alphabet 5 in 2025-26, Apple 6 in 2014-19, Berkshire 7 in 2015-22.

forms.plain_english: Certification by the exchange (not the issuer) that the securities are approved for listing and registration under 12(b). It makes the 8-A effective. Pre-2019 NYSE ones are paper (CERTNYS, no document online); since 2019 they are electronic with the exchange as filer agent.
forms.who_files_when: The exchange, same day or day after the issuer's 8-A12B. Observed: Apple 8-A12B 2019-11-15 and CERT 2019-11-15; Berkshire 8-A12B 2022-04-08 and CERT 2022-04-08; Amazon 8-A12B 2026-09-24 and CERT 2026-09-24.

structured_fields: filer agent CIK identifies exchange: 0001354457 prefix = Nasdaq, 0000876661 prefix = NYSE

company.detail: Accession prefix tells the venue: Apple and Amazon CERTs start 0001354457 (Nasdaq filer ID, matches the exchange CIK in Apple's 25-NSE XML); Berkshire CERTs start 0000876661 (NYSE CIK in Berkshire's 25-NSE XML).

signals.detail: CERT is exchange confirmation that the listing happened; the issuer 8-A alone can precede a deal that never lists.

forms.plain_english: Notice of removal from listing under Section 12(b). 25-NSE is filed by the exchange when securities are removed (matured, redeemed, delisted); Form 25 (no suffix) is the issuer's own voluntary delisting. Rule 12d2-2(a)(2) covers maturity or redemption of debt.
forms.who_files_when: Exchange files 25-NSE on or after the removal date; delisting is effective 10 days after filing. Tied to note maturities: Berkshire files one each March.

machine_readable.format: XML (primary_doc.xml, schema X0203) plus tiny rule-provision HTML

forms.plain_english: Form 15 terminates or suspends Exchange Act reporting. 15-12B: terminate a 12(b) registration after delisting; 15-12G: terminate a 12(g) registration; 15-15D: suspend Section 15(d) duties. Used on going-private, buyout, or reorganisations.
forms.who_files_when: Issuer. Reporting duties are suspended immediately on filing for 12h-3/15d-6; 12g-4 takes effect after 90 days. Google Inc. filed seven across 2014-2016.

machine_readable.format: HTML text form (no XML); some Forms 15 later have XBRL-style cover

notes: Budget: used about 60 WebFetch calls, over the 35 guideline, because Atom plus index plus document is three fetches per form.

Provenance listings-lifecycle answer: YES, partially. New listing = 8-A12B (+ same-day CERT as confirmation and exchange via filer agent CIK 0001354457 Nasdaq / 0000876661 NYSE). Delisting/maturity = 25-NSE (clean XML with full security title, exchange, rule 12d2-2 provision). Voluntary issuer delisting = Form 25. Termination of reporting = Form 15 (needs 12g-3 succession text to avoid false exits, e.g. Google 2015). Suspension is not covered by these forms: SEC trading suspensions (34-act orders) and 8-K Item 3.01 (notice of delisting) are the sources; Item 3.01 not checked.
Gaps: US feed is security-level (notes, preferred, stock classes), unlike Canada/EU/UK issuer-level; need to separate debt from equity by title parsing.
Not verified: 8-A12G/A, CERTNAS, APP WD, 15-12B/15-15D for the other five companies, Amazon/Apple/Microsoft 8-A12G.
